scope: Complete schematic eight-ball thrust bearing with eight rolling separators. Contact geometry is a modern interpretation of Madrid I20v, not a manufactured reconstruction of a museum model.

date.note: Approximate manuscript dating, not a dated completion record.

folio.verification_note: Edition foliation and text verified through e-Leo. Original-holder service may be unavailable. e-Leo viewer is an authorised-edition resource, not the original holding institution.

scale_m.note: Full swept bound. All chosen dimensions are modern explanatory assumptions, never claimed measurements of a historical machine. Measured on the rebuilt bearing: the cage's outer ring sweeps a radius of 0.446 m and the handles 0.445 m, the sills reach 0.44 m; the upper plate's top stands at 0.31 m, the ground at -0.05 m.

frame.transforms: All part positions relative to their named parent. Joint q is an extra rotation or translation about the declared parent-frame pivot applied to the rest transform. Children inherit it once.

assumptions.statement: Every numerical part size, position, orientation and support arrangement in parts is a declared modern modelling choice unless a separate primary source is explicitly attached. Materials marked assumed are plausible period choices. They are not measured from any museum replica.
assumptions.reason: Leonardo did not provide a manufacturing drawing with all dimensions.

assumptions.statement: The stated rates and loads are slow modern demonstration choices. They do not reproduce a measured speed in Leonardo s workshop.
assumptions.reason: No historical operating record was located.

assumptions.statement: The cage has eight iron pins of radius 0.004 m driven radially from an outer octagonal ring through the wheels' bores of radius 0.006 m into a turned hub, with an inner octagonal ring between the hub and the balls. The fixed iron post has radius 0.014 m; the hub is bored to radius 0.0162 m and the upper plate's iron bush to 0.0155 m. The plates are three boards each. These are modern supporting details, not measured manuscript dimensions.
assumptions.reason: Complete the numerical modern demonstration without presenting invented details as Leonardo dimensions.

input_rate.note: A demonstrator continuously turns q-top at0.833rpm. The carrier runs at half its rate by ideal equal-radius plate contact.

drive.justification: A demonstrator continuously turns q-top at0.833rpm. The carrier runs at half its rate by ideal equal-radius plate contact.

motion.visitor_12s: The top turns60degrees and the ball centres30degrees. External hand input continues. Unwrapped rotations carry across loops.

animation_notes: No bounce, no hidden energy recharge and no invisible reset.
All independent joints are in the schedule. Rigid descendants follow their parent.
Use the specified SI time without cinematic speed-up.

Plate contacts are ideal no-slip rolling. Separator spin matches the equatorial contact only and permits slip elsewhere on its curved surface. Do not describe the separator pair as an exact conjugate gear. The constant externally supplied drive replaces unmodelled friction losses.

research.identification: Madrid I20v verified in e-Leo. BNE leaflet names26r as another bearing sheet. It does not correct20v [EL-BEAR,BNE-LEAF].
research.sheet_vs_reconstruction: Leonardo names eight wooden balls and eight pivoted wheels [EL-BEAR]. Etruria Musei made a2010 model [BEARING-M]. Plates, sizes and separator profile here are modern. The octagonal ring of bars round the balls follows the sheet's drawing; its sizes, the hub, the pins, the sleeves, the boarded plates, the handles and the sills are ours.
research.dimensions: “son palle di legnio” [EL-BEAR] specifies wood, not dimensions. No numerical size or Richter number verified. No braccio conversion applies.

claims.claimed_by_leonardo: Keep balls positioned while allowing turning [EL-BEAR].
claims.tested_by_leonardo: No dated experiment by Leonardo was verified in the sources listed here. This is an evidence gap, not proof that he never tried it.
claims.built_in_lifetime: No lifetime build record located.2010 model is later [BEARING-M].
claims.later_tests: No measured friction coefficient or service-life test was located. The modern model is not such a test [BEARING-M].

physics.limits: Ideal plate rolling. Separator off-equator slip, contact stress, wood compliance and wear are not solved.
physics.verdict_en: Rolling separates the contact motion, but does not abolish friction.
physics.verdict_de: Abrollen verändert die Kontaktbewegung, beseitigt die Reibung aber nicht.

myths.claim: A frictionless modern bearing invented in finished form
myths.correction: The sheet is a study with wooden balls, not a precision steel bearing [EL-BEAR].

research.confidence: High folio and material. ClassC numerical interpretation. Medium ideal plate kinematics, unresolved separator friction.
